_meta.description: Tactical patterns and motifs — common combinations to watch for
_meta.match_strategy: Pattern type detected from PV line analysis

undefended_piece.name: Undefended Pieces
undefended_piece.rule: Before EVERY move, check: Are any of my pieces undefended?
undefended_piece.explanation: Many tactics work because a piece was left undefended. An undefended piece is a target for forks, discovered attacks, and double attacks.
undefended_piece.prevention: After deciding your move, do a final 'blunder check' — scan all your pieces.

pin_to_king.name: Pin to the King
pin_to_king.trigger: Piece on line between attacker and king
pin_to_king.rule: Avoid placing valuable pieces on lines with your king.
pin_to_king.explanation: A pinned piece cannot move without exposing the king to check. The pinned piece is essentially paralyzed.
pin_to_king.prevention: Before developing a piece, check if it will be on the same file/diagonal as your king.

pin_to_queen.name: Pin to the Queen
pin_to_queen.trigger: Piece on line between attacker and queen
pin_to_queen.rule: Watch for bishops and rooks that line up with your queen.
pin_to_queen.explanation: A relative pin (to the queen) doesn't prevent movement, but moving the pinned piece loses the queen.
pin_to_queen.prevention: Keep your queen off exposed diagonals and files where she can be pinned.

knight_fork.name: Knight Fork
knight_fork.trigger: Knight attacks multiple valuable pieces simultaneously
knight_fork.rule: Watch for knight fork squares when your king and queen are on the same color complex.
knight_fork.explanation: Knights can attack multiple pieces at once. The most deadly forks target king and queen simultaneously.
knight_fork.prevention: After every opponent knight move, check what squares it attacks. Can it fork your pieces?

pawn_fork.name: Pawn Fork
pawn_fork.trigger: Pawn advance attacks two pieces diagonally
pawn_fork.rule: Watch for pawn advances that attack two pieces at once.
pawn_fork.explanation: A pawn fork is devastating because the pawn is worth the least — you always profit.
pawn_fork.prevention: Don't place two pieces on adjacent files where a pawn can attack both.

back_rank_weakness.name: Back Rank Mate
back_rank_weakness.trigger: King trapped on back rank with no escape squares
back_rank_weakness.rule: Give your king an escape square (luft) — push h6 or g6.
back_rank_weakness.explanation: If your king has no escape and your back rank is weak, a rook or queen delivers mate.
back_rank_weakness.prevention: Create luft (h3/g3 or h6/g6) before it's too late. Do it during a quiet moment.

discovered_attack.name: Discovered Attack
discovered_attack.trigger: Piece moves to reveal an attack by another piece behind it
discovered_attack.rule: Watch for pieces lined up behind your pieces — moving one reveals the other.
discovered_attack.explanation: Discovered attacks are powerful because you make two threats at once. The moving piece attacks one target while uncovering an attack on another.
discovered_attack.prevention: Check for enemy pieces lurking behind other pieces on your key lines.

discovered_check.name: Discovered Check
discovered_check.trigger: Piece moves to reveal check from a piece behind it
discovered_check.rule: Discovered check is one of the most powerful tactical motifs.
discovered_check.explanation: The piece giving the discovered check forces the king to move, while the moving piece can capture anything freely.
discovered_check.prevention: Avoid placing your king on the same line as enemy long-range pieces with blockers.

skewer.name: Skewer
skewer.trigger: Valuable piece attacked, and a less valuable piece behind it on the same line
skewer.rule: Keep your valuable pieces off the same diagonal/file/rank.
skewer.explanation: A skewer is a reverse pin — the more valuable piece must move, exposing the less valuable one behind.
skewer.prevention: After each move, check if your king/queen is on the same line as another piece.

overloaded_piece.name: Overloaded Piece
overloaded_piece.trigger: One piece defending two or more critical things simultaneously
overloaded_piece.rule: If one piece is doing too many jobs, something will break.
overloaded_piece.explanation: An overloaded piece can't defend everything. Attack one of its responsibilities, and the others collapse.
overloaded_piece.prevention: Distribute defensive duties across multiple pieces. Don't rely on one piece for everything.

deflection.name: Deflection
deflection.trigger: A piece is lured away from defending a critical square or piece
deflection.rule: Force the defender away from its duty, then strike.
deflection.explanation: Deflection forces a key defender to abandon its post by attacking it or offering a sacrifice.
deflection.prevention: Identify your key defenders and ensure they can't be lured away.

decoy.name: Decoy
decoy.trigger: A piece is lured to a bad square where it becomes vulnerable
decoy.rule: Don't take gifts blindly — check if the square is a trap.
decoy.explanation: A decoy sacrifice lures the enemy piece to a specific square where a tactic then works.
decoy.prevention: Before capturing, ask: Why is my opponent offering this? What happens on this square?

trapped_piece.name: Trapped Piece
trapped_piece.trigger: A piece has no safe squares to move to
trapped_piece.rule: Always have an escape route for your pieces, especially bishops and knights.
trapped_piece.explanation: A trapped piece is one that has no safe squares. It will be captured even if it's currently defended.
trapped_piece.prevention: Before advancing a piece deep into enemy territory, ensure it has a retreat.

double_attack.name: Double Attack
double_attack.trigger: A single move creates two threats simultaneously
double_attack.rule: The strongest moves create multiple threats. Look for double attacks.
double_attack.explanation: A double attack forces your opponent to choose which threat to address — they can't deal with both.
double_attack.prevention: After opponent moves, count ALL the threats, not just the most obvious one.

interference.name: Interference
interference.trigger: A piece blocks the connection between two enemy pieces
interference.rule: If two enemy pieces protect each other on a line, block the connection.
interference.explanation: Interference breaks the coordination between enemy pieces by placing a piece on the connecting line.
interference.prevention: Keep defensive lines clear. Don't rely on distant pieces protecting each other.

zwischenzug.name: Zwischenzug (In-Between Move)
zwischenzug.trigger: An unexpected intermediate move before the expected recapture
zwischenzug.rule: Before recapturing, check if there's a stronger move first.
zwischenzug.explanation: An in-between move (usually a check or serious threat) before the expected recapture changes the position favorably.
zwischenzug.prevention: After a capture, don't automatically recapture. Look for checks and threats first.

removing_the_defender.name: Removing the Defender
removing_the_defender.trigger: Capturing or chasing a piece that defends a key square or piece
removing_the_defender.rule: If something is defended by only one piece, attack the defender.
removing_the_defender.explanation: Remove the defender and the whole position collapses. Target the piece that holds everything together.
removing_the_defender.prevention: Ensure critical squares and pieces have multiple defenders.
